title: continuous batcher: tail-latency SLA mitigation and starvation prevention
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Reduces tail latency in continuous batching by adding starvation guards, per-priority timeouts, and lightweight preemptive flushing; no API changes.
commits_summary: 3 commits: tuning: add dequeue-time-tracker and priority-wakeup; scheduler: per-priority timeout and preemptive flush; tests: add sim harness for starvation scenarios
description: Context: In production we observed priority inversion and multi-minute tail spikes from continuous batching under mixed workloads where long-running low-priority requests could starve high-priority short requests. Goal: reduce p99 tail latency for high-priority traffic without materially reducing throughput or increasing cost. Summary of changes: 1) dequeue-time-tracker: per-request enqueue timestamp and lightweight slot-age counters to detect oldest-waiting requests without atomic contention; 2) per-priority timeout policy: configurable thresholds (default: high=50ms, normal=150ms, low=400ms) that trigger preemptive flush of the current batch to admit waiting older requests; 3) priority-wakeup: when an older request crosses its timeout we mark the worker to prefer building a batch that includes that request on next cycle; 4) minimal KV cache interaction: we do not evict KV entries on preemptive flush, we reuse prefix KV and mark batches as "non-merged" for cache accounting; 5) metrics and observability: batch_queue_time_p50/p95/p99 per-priority, preemptive_flush_count, blocked_slots_gauge, and an e2e span to trace preemptive flush decisions. Rationale and design notes: the implementation biases towards fairness rather than strict deadline scheduling to avoid oscillation; timeouts are applied per-priority and use exponential backoff to avoid cascade flush storms; dequeue-time-tracker uses per-shard accumulation to avoid hot atomics on high QPS. Tests and results: unit tests cover timeout transitions and KV cache flags; integration smoke added for preemptive flush path; a synthetic load sim (runtime/tests/batcher_starvation_sim.cc + bench driver) emulates 128 clients with a 10% high-priority short (8-12ms) and 90% low-priority long (300-800ms). Baseline p99 for high-priority was 420ms under sustained load. After changes baseline p99 dropped to 120ms, p50 improved from 68ms to 22ms, throughput variance <2%. Observability: dashboards added in docs/observability/batcher_metrics.md and example alert rule: alert if preemptive_flush_count rate > 100/s for 5m. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked ENG-3124 - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] perf sims and benchmark config - [x] docs for metrics - [x] backwards-compatible config defaults Rollout plan: start with Canary on Dedicated pool with feature flag continuous_batcher.preemptive_flush=opt-in. Monitor p99 and preemptive_flush_count for 1 hour, then enable for wider pools. Fallback: feature flag off returns to previous behavior; no model-serving API changes. Files changed (high level): continuous_scheduler core: add timeout checks and wake flags; dequeue_tracker: new header + light-weight sharded counters; timeout_policy: policy and config; metrics_registry: new per-priority metrics; tests and benchmarks. Review conversation: Marco Ortega: "Can you quantify cost impact of more frequent flushes?" Priya Raman: "Measured throughput variance <2% in our sim; realtime billing estimate shows <0.5% extra token cost at target workloads; included bench configs to reproduce." Liang Chen: "Need to ensure no contention regression on hot paths." Priya Raman: "dequeue-time-tracker uses per-shard accumulators and only samples queue head every N cycles; added microbenchmarks showing <3% overhead at 10k qps." Sasha Petrov: "Can preemptive flush interact with autoscaler briefer than expected?" Priya Raman: "Autoscaler uses CPU/GPU utilization signals; preemptive flush increases per-request scheduling decisions but not sustained GPU utilization; recommended to monitor the autoscaler window during canary." Code review requests: Liang requested small refactor to reduce virtual calls in timeout_policy; addressed in second commit. CI: initial run had lint failure on docs; fixed and rerun; final status: linux-build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-smoke: pass, perf-ci: pass, lint: pass. Merge notes: approved by all reviewers on 2026-02-27; merged via squash on 2026-02-28. Related work: complements ENG-3178 (kv-cache-aware batching) and should be considered when enabling quantization-driven kernel selection to avoid longer kernel runtimes causing tail regression. Notes for on-call: if alerts for preemptive_flush_count spike while p99 not improving, revert via feature flag and open ENG follow-up. Linear links: ENG-3124 design, ENG-3178 follow-up.
